# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

**Investigated**: The format rules for m:ss and h:mm:ss timer strings. The existing parseCompound helper and its undefined-versus-throw convention. The Node test suite, typecheck, and Biome lint and format results after the change.

**Learned**: New helpers use an undefined-return convention, so parseClock returns undefined for invalid input and never throws. parseCompound still throws TypeError, and the parseCompound JSDoc says so. In m:ss the leading minutes field accepts any number of digits, so 90:00 is valid. Seconds, and minutes in h:mm:ss, must be two digits from 00 to 59. Negatives, fractional seconds, surrounding whitespace, and one-digit seconds all return undefined.

**Completed**: parseClock is implemented and exported from src/index.ts. parseClock('1:30') returns 90000 and parseClock('01:02:03') returns 3723000. Its tests are in src/parse-clock.test.ts. All six Jest suites pass (205 tests) with 100% coverage. tsc --noEmit, biome lint, and biome format are clean. The edge-runtime tests (test:edge) were not run.

**Next Steps**: Decide whether to add a README section for parseClock next to the parseCompound section. The user has not yet asked for one.

**Notes**: The parseCompound length-guard off-by-one is still open: the code allows up to 100 characters while its message and JSDoc say 1 to 99. parseClock's format rules were chosen by the agent because the user did not specify them, so the user should confirm them. The API now mixes conventions: parseCompound and parse differ, and parseClock follows the undefined-return convention.
